demos.title: Label the fictional output
scenes: Inspect the proposed output
Unfamiliar wording → lower priority. One-day completion → promised.
Fictional draft for review. Neither rule is established.
Label the parts
Promise: claim • Wording rule: assumption • Deadline: context
A confident sentence is not supporting evidence.
Compare the supplied policy
Use stated deadline and work impact; refer uncertainty for review.
No writing-style criterion or completion guarantee is supplied.

demos.title: Compare two equivalent requests
scenes: Hold the task facts constant
Two form copies • Friday 2 p.m. • Same office meeting
Only phrasing changes between the two fictional inputs.
Compare A and B
A: complete sentence. B: brief phrasing. Same task facts.
Expected: use the same stated deadline and work-impact criteria.
Save the actual comparison
Record priority, reason and next action for each response.
A difference needs examination; a match is evidence for this test only.

demos.title: Test a conflicting deadline
scenes: Introduce one error case
Requested: Friday 2 p.m. Meeting note: Monday morning.
No resolved calendar date or confirmed deadline is supplied.
Set the expected boundary
Flag the conflict. Ask for clarification. Human review before final routing.
Do not invent a date, permission or service promise.
Inspect the actual response
Did it flag the conflict, or guess and route anyway?
Save the result, correction and retest; keep uncertainty visible.

demos.title: Correct the rule and name its limits
scenes: Make a material correction
Remove wording-based priority and the unsupported one-day promise.
Correct the decision rule, not just the tone.
Retest the same cases
Equivalent A • Equivalent B • Conflicting deadline
Save actual responses. Mark an unrun retest as pending.
Keep the finding bounded
Verified finding • Unresolved question • Proposed action
Retain limits and the human decision; no universal fairness certificate.
